title: Leaf-Level Gas Exchange Measurement for Photosynthesis Model Calibration
author: Kyle T. Rizzo

steps.title: Verify Ambient Conditions
steps.instruction: Ensure field conditions are suitable for model calibration to maximize effectiveness.

substeps.instruction: Verify full sun with minimal cloud coverage and minimal wind.
Confirm daily high air temperature is at least 18°C (65°F).
Target ambient light reaching 2000 μmol m⁻² s⁻¹ and leaf vapor pressure difference ranges of 10-30 mmol mol⁻¹.
Perform measurements between mid-morning and solar noon.

steps.title: Perform LI-6800 Initial Setup
steps.instruction: Configure the instrument hardware and software settings before the measurement session.

substeps.instruction: Connect the head (hand-held unit) via cable and tube.
Install the largest aperture size that can be consistently covered by the sampled leaves; select the corresponding size in 'Start up' → 'Chamber Setup'.
Check 'Add Dynamic Equations' in 'Start up' → 'Chamber Setup'.
Synchronize the clock via 'Start up' → 'System Setting' → 'Date Time & Clocks' → 'Sync Head Clock'.
Enable 'UseDynamic' in 'Constants' → 'Gas Exchange'.
Connect the H₂O add column and ensure it is sufficiently filled with water.
Check desiccant level; replace Sorbead® (orange) or Drierite® (blue) if less than 1/2 remains.
Remove the red cover from the light sensor.

steps.title: Configure Initial Environment Settings
steps.instruction: Close the empty chamber and set the following parameters in the 'Environment' tab:

substeps.instruction: Flow: Auto - 500 μmol/mol
Overpressure: Auto - 0.1 kPa
Pump speed: Auto
RH_air: 50%
CO2_r: 400 μmol/mol
Soda Lime Scrub: Auto
Fan Speed: 10,000 rpm
Temperature: Off
Head Light Source Setpoint: 2,000 μmol/m²/s

steps.title: Calibrate IRGAs and Dynamic Tuning
steps.instruction: Perform point matching, range matching, and dynamic tuning for CO₂ and H₂O.

substeps.instruction: Point Matching: In 'Measurements' tab, click 'Match IRGAs' → 'Auto'. Wait for both CO₂ and H₂O lights to turn green.
Range Matching: In 'Constants' → 'Range Match', click 'CO2 Range Match' → 'Start' (Normal 5 min match, Flow s/Flow r = 1.13). Repeat for H₂O using the Quick 3 min match.
Dynamic Tuning: In 'Constants' → 'Dynamic', ensure CO₂ and H₂O control are on. In 'Utilities/Tests', run 'CO2 Test Current' → 'Start', wait 2 min, and store. Repeat for 'H2O Test Current'.

steps.title: Collect A-Ci Response Curves
steps.instruction: Collect A-Ci curve measurements for each temperature and light combination specified in the study design (e.g., Table 3).

substeps.instruction: Select a healthy, fully-expanded, outer-canopy sunlit leaf and clamp the chamber, ensuring the aperture is entirely covered.
Choose a measurement method: Manual or Automated.

If Manual: Create a crop-specific folder, open a log file ({YYYY-MM-DD}_{time}_Q{light}_T{temperature}), set air temperature (e.g., 25, 30, 35°C), and set light flux (e.g., 2000, 1600, 1200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹).
If Automated: Transfer .py scripts (e.g., ACi_Light_Sweep.py) from USB to the LI-6800 BP Directory via 'Tools' → 'Manage Files'. Add user variables 'CurveID' and 'Response' in 'Constants' → 'User'.
Wait for all environmental set-points to reach the green 7/7 badge.

Run the A-Ci curve: In 'Programs' → 'BP Builder', select 'dynamic/DAT CO2 continuous.py' and start with: Starting CO₂ 200 μmol/mol, Pre-ramp Wait 1 min, Ending CO₂ 2,000 μmol/mol, Ramp rate 300 μmol/mol, and Logging interval 3 sec.
Monitor the curve in real-time (A vs Ci) to ensure it forms an increasing hyperbola. Save the log file and repeat for subsequent light/temperature combinations.

steps.title: Perform Survey Measurements
steps.instruction: Collect survey measurements on 15–25 randomly selected healthy, sunlit, fully-expanded leaves to capture canopy variability.

substeps.instruction: Perform CO₂ and H₂O point matching again.
Open a log file named {YYYY-MM-DD}_{time}_A_survey.
Set air temperature to 25°C and light flux to 2000 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
Ensure other environment values match the survey requirements (Table 5) and wait for the green 7/7 badge.
Clamp the chamber onto a leaf and wait for the A reading to stabilize (less than 3% deviation over 10 seconds, typically 30s to 2min).
Record the measurement using the 'Log' button on the head handle or console.
Repeat for all 15–25 leaves.

steps.title: Re-scale Data and Fit Model
steps.instruction: Re-scale the A-Ci curves using survey statistics and fit the data to a photosynthetic model (e.g., FvCB).

substeps.instruction: Calculate the re-scaling factor using the median saturated A from survey measurements at reference temperature (Tref = 25°C) and light (Qin = 2000 μmol m⁻² s⁻¹).
Apply the formula: Ai,scaled = Ai * (median(Asat,Tref,survey) / Asat,Tref,response).
Use a fitting tool such as PhoTorch Studio to upload LI-6800 files, apply re-scaling, and extract model parameters (e.g., Vcmax, Jmax, TPU).

description: Software The protocol can be semi-automated with Background Programs written for the LI-6800. Three programs are provided, one that carries out the light sweep, one that carries out the temperature sweep, and one that carries out light sweep followed by the temperature sweep. The protocol can also be applied without the automation script by manually varying each environmental setpoint and running the CO 2 response program already included in the instrument firmware. In addition to the data collection, we also discuss parameter calibration based on PhoTorch (Lei et al. 2025). List of optional software: LI-6800 Background Programs for automated measurements of light and temperature sweeps ( https://github.com/PlantSimulationLab/LI6800-automated-scripts) PhoTorch ( https://github.com/GEMINI-Breeding/photorch), for advanced users looking to automate workflows of fitting large datasets with Python PhoTorch Studio ( https://github.com/ktrizzo/photorch-studio), for simple drag-and-drop fitting with a graphical user interface (Automated Option) Run the light-sweep Background Program in ‘ Programs ’ → ‘ BP Builder ’. Browse to the location of the downloaded program ACi_Light_Sweep.py , select it, and press ‘ Start BP ’. Use the default settings. Allow the program to run for 40 minutes. Close the log file. (Automated Option) Run the temperature-sweep Background Program in ‘ Programs ’ → ‘ BP Builder ’. Browse to the location of the downloaded program ACi_Temperature_Sweep.py , select it, and press ‘ Start BP ’. Use the default settings. Allow the program to run for 50 minutes. Close the log file.
